experiments.assumption: Registration for a termiticide edge sealant is affordable or avoidable
experiments.hypothesis: A registered wood preservative can be used as-is, or registration costs under ₹3 lakh and 12 months.
experiments.method: One paid consultation with an agrochemical regulatory consultant, plus a check of registered wood-preservative products.
experiments.success_criteria: clear path under ₹3 lakh and 12 months
experiments.failure_criteria: path over 12 months or unknown cost

experiments.assumption: Carpenters will apply it to every edge without supervision
experiments.hypothesis: At least 4 of 5 carpenters reach 95% UV-visible edge coverage on a real job.
experiments.method: Give 5 carpenters a hand-mixed kit (borate product plus tracer) and inspect their next job with a UV torch.

experiments.assumption: A board maker would license the tracer idea
experiments.hypothesis: At least one board maker's product team asks for a trial.
experiments.method: Send a one-page proposal to two board makers' product teams.

experiments.assumption: Brackets and anchors hold a loaded tall wardrobe safely
experiments.hypothesis: No bracket deforms more than 2 mm and no anchor pulls out at 3x expected load.
experiments.method: Sandbag load test on brick and AAC walls for 24 hours with two prototype sets.

experiments.assumption: Carpenters will pay a price that covers cost
experiments.hypothesis: At least 4 of 10 carpenters say they would pay ₹3,500 or more per set and quote it to clients.
experiments.method: Show the prototype to 10 carpenters; ask what they would pay and whether clients would accept it.

experiments.assumption: Termites reach built-ins mainly through walls and floors
experiments.hypothesis: Most pest-control technicians report wall or floor contact as the usual entry route in apartments.
experiments.method: Interview 5 pest-control technicians about entry routes they find in built-in furniture.
experiments.success_criteria: most cite wall or floor contact
experiments.failure_criteria: most cite infested boards or other routes

experiments.assumption: Homeowners will pay for remote verification
experiments.hypothesis: At least 5 of 20 homeowners pay ₹499 for a 30-minute video check of delivered boards.
experiments.method: Offer the paid video check through two interior designers; messages and any booking page need user approval.

experiments.hypothesis: At least 2 of 5 designers agree to refer clients.

experiments.assumption: Inspections find problems homeowners care about
experiments.hypothesis: At least 2 of the first 10 checks find a mismatch the homeowner acts on.
experiments.method: Record every mismatch found in the first 10 checks and whether the homeowner acted.
